0.0.n: Politely points out the appetizers being presented.

0.1.n: A small starter served automatically at many Japanese pubs, usually with a charge.

0.2.n: Part of でございます, a very polite version of です.

0.3.n: The stem of ございます; together with で, it forms a very polite way to identify something.

0.4.n: Completes でございます, giving the sentence a formal service tone.

1.0.n: Politely acknowledges what the server has said.

2.0.n: お adds politeness to 好き when referring to the customer's preference.

2.1.n: Connects 好き to の, allowing the description to refer to a particular item.

2.2.n: Stands in for an unnamed item: something you like.

2.3.n: Combines with つ to make 一つ, the general counting word for one item.

2.4.n: With 1, forms 一つ, used to count one thing without naming its category.

3.0.n: Literally means what; here it asks which appetizer is popular.

3.1.n: Marks 何 as the thing whose popularity is being asked about.

3.2.n: Describes an item that many customers choose or like.

3.4.n: Turns the polite statement into a question.

4.1.n: Says that all the choices are liked by customers.

4.2.n: Connects 人気 to the explanatory んです construction.

4.3.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before the speaker offers recommendations.

4.4.n: Makes the explanation in んです polite.

4.5.n: Softens the transition from saying everything is popular to naming particular choices.

4.7.n: A conversational pause that makes the recommendation sound less definite.

4.9.n: Literally names the bird, but here it is shorthand for its eggs.

4.10.n: Links the ingredient うずら to 燻製, identifying what has been smoked.

4.11.n: Names a food prepared by smoking; here the ingredient is quail eggs.

4.14.n: This segment is part of いぶりがっこ, the name of a smoked radish pickle, not a separate verb here.

4.15.n: The こ completes いぶりがっこ; the following か marks it as another option.

5.0.n: Begins a drawn-out reaction showing recognition or understanding.

5.1.n: Continues the same reaction; ー indicates that the vowel is held longer.

6.0.n: Adds another category to the server's recommendations.

6.1.n: Describes the preparation method of the foods mentioned next.

6.2.n: Combines with 燻製 to refer broadly to foods prepared by smoking.

6.3.n: Marks the smoked items as the subject, but the speaker leaves the description unfinished.

7.0.n: Introduces a decision based on what the server has just said.

7.1.n: Frames this as an initial choice, leaving room for further decisions.

7.3.n: Refers back to the smoked quail eggs; the object marker を is omitted in casual speech.

7.4.n: A polite, humble form of もらう used here to accept or order the selected dish.

8.2.n: Expresses gratitude; adding ございます makes it more polite.

8.3.n: The stem of ございます, used here as part of the formal thank-you expression.

8.4.n: Completes ございます, making the expression suitable for customer service.

0.tip: でございます is a very polite version of です, common in customer service.

1.tip: はい can acknowledge what someone says without necessarily expressing agreement.

2.lit: One of the ones you like...
2.tip: 好きなの means one you like; the request to choose is left unstated.

3.tip: 何が asks which thing has the quality being discussed.

4.lit: All are popular, but, well, smoked quail eggs or smoked pickled daikon or...
4.tip: か lists alternatives here rather than marking a question.

5.tip: The drawn-out ああ signals that the listener is taking in the explanation.

6.tip: The sentence trails off after が, leaving the description of the smoked items implied.

7.lit: Then, for now, I'll take quail eggs.
7.tip: いただきます can politely mean I'll take it when choosing food, not only when starting a meal.

8.tip: ありがとうございます is the polite thank-you expression commonly used by staff with customers.
